classification.difficultyReason: The hardest part requires relating two ratios after equal additions, by recognising an unchanged difference or constructing an equation. The male-fraction part also requires combining subgroup proportions with the unequal student and staff totals.

inlines.text: The ratio of students to staff in a school trip is

children.label: a
children.prompt: What are the possible total number of staff and students on the trip?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Total parts}&=25+3\\&=28\end{align*}$$
The total must be a positive whole-number multiple of 28: $28,56,84,\ldots$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: There are 12 members of staff. Some students then cancel. The ratio is now $15:2$. How many students cancelled?

answer.worked:
Initially, 3 parts represent 12 staff.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=12\div3=4\\\text{Initial students}&=25\times4=100\end{align*}$$
After cancellations, 2 parts represent the same 12 staff.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=12\div2=6\\\text{Remaining students}&=15\times6=90\\\text{Students cancelled}&=100-90=10\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: At the last minute, 15 extra students and 15 extra staff join. The new ratio is $40:7$. How many students and staff were there to begin with?

answer.worked:
Adding equal numbers leaves the difference between students and staff unchanged. Express both ratios with a difference of 66 parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Initial ratio}&=25:3=75:9\\\text{New ratio}&=40:7=80:14\\\text{Initial difference}&=75-9=66\\\text{New difference}&=80-14=66\end{align*}$$
The increase is 5 parts for each group, representing 15 people.
$$\begin{align*}1\text{ part}&=15\div5=3\\\text{Initial students}&=75\times3=225\\\text{Initial staff}&=9\times3=27\end{align*}$$
Check: $240:42=40:7$ after adding 15 to each group.

children.label: d
children.prompt: The ratio of male to female students is $8:7$ and the ratio of male to female staff is $4:5$. What fraction of the total are male?

answer.worked:
Use the equivalent students-to-staff ratio $75:9$, so each group can be divided into its male and female parts.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Male students}&=75\div(8+7)\times8\\&=40\\\text{Male staff}&=9\div(4+5)\times4\\&=4\\\text{Fraction male}&=\frac{40+4}{75+9}\\&=\frac{44}{84}\\&=\frac{11}{21}\end{align*}$$
